messages.content: Help me obtain an InputSource for the entity with a system identifier 'http://astro.com/stylesheets/toptemplate' when parsing an XML document using a SAX filter factory, with publicid '1234'?

function.name: SAXFilterFactoryImpl_resolveEntity
function.description: Resolves an entity using its public identifier and system identifier. If the system identifier matches a specific known value, it returns a new InputSource with the system ID converted to a URL; otherwise, it returns null to use the default behavior. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

publicid.description: The public identifier of the entity to resolve. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

sysId.description: The system identifier of the entity to resolve. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

message.content:
Below is a minimal but complete illustration of **how to supply your own `InputSource`** for the DTD/entity whose *system* URI is  
```
http://astro.com/stylesheets/toptemplate
```  
when you’re building a SAX‑filter chain.  

---

### 1️⃣ What you actually need

When the SAX parser encounters an external entity reference, it asks an `EntityResolver`.  
If you return `null`, the parser falls back to the default resolution mechanism (usually a local copy or a remote fetch).  
To force the parser to read the entity from wherever you like – e.g., a bundled stylesheet, a cached file, or even a hard‑coded string – simply build an `InputSource` yourself and hand it back.

In your case the public ID is `"1234"` and the system ID is the long HTTP URL shown above.  
All you have to do is detect that exact system ID inside `resolveEntity()` and construct an appropriate `InputSource`.

---

### 2️⃣ Sample implementation

Here’s a ready‑to‑copy Java snippet that shows everything from creating the resolver to wiring it up to a SAX filter factory.

> ```java
> import org.xml.sax.*;
> import org.xml.sax.helpers.DefaultHandler;
> 
> import javax.xml.parsers.SAXParser;
> import javax.xml.parsers.SAXParserFactory;
> import java.io.InputStream;
> import java.net.URL;
> 
> /**
>  * Custom EntityResolver that knows about one special system ID.
>  */
> public class AstroEntityResolver implements EntityResolver {
>     private static final String TARGET_SYSID =
>             "http://astro.com/stylesheets/toptemplate";
> 
>     @Override
>     public InputSource resolveEntity(String publicId, String systemId)
>             throws IOException, SAXException {
>         System.out.println(
>                 "Requested entity -> publicId=" + publicId +
>                         ", systemId=" + systemId);
>
>         /* Check whether this is the entity we care about … */
>         if ("1234".equals(publicId) && TARGET_SYSID.equals(systemId)) {
>             /*
>              * You can now decide where to get the data:
>              *
>              * • From the web → new URL(systemId).openStream()
>              * • From the JAR/classpath → ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream(...)
>              * • Hard‑code a small fragment as a ByteArrayInputStream …
>              */
>             
>             // Example: pull it straight off the internet
>             try (InputStream stream = new URL(TARGET_SYSID).openConnection().getInputStream()) {
>                 InputSource src = new InputSource(stream);
>                 src.setPublicId(publicId);   // optional but nice
>                 src.setSystemId(systemId);   // keep original system ID
>                 return src;
>             }
>         }
>         
>         /* For all other cases let the parser fall back to defaults */
>         return null;
>     }
> }
> ```

#### How to plug it into a SAX filter factory

Assuming you already have a `XMLReader` (e.g., obtained from a `SAXParser`) and you wish to add a filter around it:

> ```java
> // Create base reader
> SAXParserFactory spf = SAXParserFactory.newInstance();
> spf.setNamespaceAware(true);
> SAXParser parser = spf.newSAXParser();
> XMLReader baseReader = parser.getXMLReader();
> 
> // Attach your resolver
> baseReader.setEntityResolver(new AstroEntityResolver());
> 
> // Wrap with whatever filters you need
> // (here we just pass through without modification)
> XMLReader filteredReader = new XMLFilterImpl(baseReader);
> 
> // Now parse something!
> filteredReader.parse("file:/tmp/example.xml");
> ```
> 

That’s literally all you need—just replace the “pull it straight off the internet” block with however you prefer to locate the stylesheet (classpath, cache directory, embedded string, etc.).

---

### 3️⃣ Why this works

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| Parser sees `<xsl:stylesheet href="toptemplate"/>` | Calls `entityResolver.resolveEntity(pubId, sysId)` |
| Your resolver checks IDs | Matches both `"1234"` & the target URL |
| Returns non‑null `InputSource` | Parser reads the supplied stream instead of trying to download again |

Because you returned a concrete `InputSource`, the parser never performs its usual lookup, guaranteeing deterministic behaviour regardless of network availability or server configuration.

---

### 4️⃣ Quick checklist before running

1. **Make sure the URL is reachable** (or adjust the resolver to serve a local fallback).
2. **Handle I/O exceptions** appropriately – the resolver may throw them upstream.
3. **Set character encoding** if needed (`src.setEncoding(...)`). By default the parser uses UTF‑8 unless overridden.
4. **Test with a simple XML** containing the entity reference to confirm the resolver fires.

Happy parsing! 🚀
